sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Polysil is not a demonstrated irrigation compounder. The FY2026 revenue rebound to ₹45.58 crore follows a collapse to ₹13.89 crore in FY2025, and remains below FY2021 revenue of ₹54.59 crore. The five-year revenue CAGR is -3.5%. Most FY2026 sales are traded goods rather than internally manufactured output. The important question is collection quality and return on new capital, not the size of India’s irrigation opportunity.

At the authenticated 19 October 2026 close of ₹49.80, current issued equity is worth ₹132.00 crore. BQS is 2.8/10 and GQS 2.2/10; IAS is NS. Financial reliability is on Hold because bank-reported current assets repeatedly differ materially from the books without an adequate explanation. This is not an accusation of fraud. The unmodified FY2026 audit and clean IFC opinion are meaningful counterevidence, but do not reconcile the disclosed differences.

The most consequential adverse facts are persistent cash burn, aged receivables, FY2025 actual loan defaults and substantial dilution. Reported FY2026 CFO of negative ₹47.58 crore overstates operating burn because ₹26.08 crore moved into bank deposits. After that correction and removing a noncash ₹2 crore prepaid-issue-cost release, adjusted CFO is still negative ₹23.51 crore. June disclosures identify ₹26.19 crore of unspent eligible issue funds, while another ₹40.34 crore depends on optional warrant exercise. Full remaining conversion increases current shares by 117.3%.

Do not initiate on the irrigation narrative or the prior share-price decline. The model’s ordinary returns and entry prices are deliberately unscored. Even the separately labeled, funded full-conversion base case generates an illustrative annual return of -26.7%, not an investment target. A repaired bank reconciliation, sustained collections and credible self-funded growth would change the analysis.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 1, DUR 4, CAP 2, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 3, EARN 3, R NS, D2, P NS and L NS. Scores answer different questions: GOV assesses stewardship, GQS means Growth Quality, and P means price-implied expectations. Valuation does not reduce BQS.

BQS = 0.20×4 + 0.20×3 + 0.12×1 + 0.10×4 + 0.12×2 + 0.10×2 + 0.08×3 + 0.08×3 = 2.84. GQS = 0.40×1 + 0.20×4 + 0.15×3 + 0.15×2 + 0.10×2 = 2.15. Persistent weak cash realization and poor incremental capital returns activate the framework’s GQS ceiling of 5; the raw 2.15 already falls below it. The ceiling is explicitly applicable, not omitted because it does not change the displayed score.

IAS retains the unrounded 2.84 BQS input. Its known contribution is 0.25×2.84 + 0.20×2 = 1.11, with 45% original-weight coverage. R, P and L remain missing, so the mathematical missing-factor range is [1.66, 6.61], not a confidence interval or investable midpoint. There is no weight redistribution and no invented 5/10. Ordinary returns are withheld under G2, and there is no favorable investment classification.

All factors have source references, evidence IDs, an adjacent-score explanation and a confidence label. Moving the two most uncertain scored business judgments, GOV and MOAT, together by one point changes raw BQS by 0.40. If GOV fell to 3 on sufficient evidence, the governance override would independently cap BQS/IAS at 3 and change the action to Avoid — governance. That is not the current finding. Display uses conventional HALF_UP one-decimal rounding only; classification uses exact unrounded totals.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Polysil manufactures and trades HDPE and LLDPE/LDPE pipes, drip systems, sprinklers, fittings and related irrigation components under the Polysil brand. Its owned Vadodara-area plant and operating history provide a real industrial base. Customers obtain water-delivery systems through distributors, dealers, institutional projects and subsidy-linked channels. The product is useful; that alone says little about the manufacturer’s pricing power or cash economics.

FY2026 revenue consists of pipes ₹33.5995 crore, sprinklers ₹1.9748 crore and drip irrigation ₹10.0069 crore. The manufacturing/trading split is more revealing: manufactured turnover is only ₹19.1268 crore, or 41.96%, while trading is ₹26.4543 crore, or 58.04%. In FY2024 manufacturing contributed ₹40.6254 crore, 91.37% of sales. Thus the recovery is not simply the old factory producing substantially more of its own product. Segment disclosure treats the business as one operating segment, but that does not erase the economic distinction between resale and production.

The IPO described nine distributors and roughly 425 dealers. Those are dated IPO-era counts, not independently verified October 2026 coverage. Farmer payments and subsidy receivables can be collected on different schedules. The prospectus described assistance often covering 50–70% of approved installation cost with collection delays, while the central government’s dated PDMC description gives 55% for small/marginal farmers and 45% for others, with state implementation differences. Do not assume every sale is subsidized or that one national percentage determines Polysil’s invoice cash flow.

The key unit economics are net realization after dealer discounts, resin/input cost, installation/service burden, subsidy collection lag, bad-debt loss and capital tied up before payment. Current unit volumes, realized prices, dealer sell-through and installation-level margins were not disclosed sufficiently to decompose price versus volume. No missing unit economics are replaced with a sector growth assumption.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Demand for water efficiency, irrigation replacement and agricultural productivity creates a genuine industry opportunity. It does not establish an issuer-specific moat. BIS compliance, a recognizable brand, plant ownership and a dealer network are useful operating prerequisites. Evidence of unusually high customer retention, protected technology, sustained price premiums or superior normalized capital returns is missing. The shift toward trading weakens the inference that manufacturing process advantages explain FY2026 growth.

Three peers illustrate different boundaries rather than provide an indiscriminate valuation average. Captain Polyplast is a closer irrigation-products comparator: FY2026 standalone revenue is ₹417.27 crore, PAT ₹27.26 crore and CFO negative ₹22.39 crore. That confirms sector collection risk is real, but Polysil’s adjusted burn of ₹23.51 crore on only ₹45.58 crore sales is much more severe relative to scale. Captain’s FY2025 PAT included a ₹15.61 crore investment-sale gain, so its reported PAT decline is not equivalent to an operating collapse.

Jain Irrigation is much larger and diversified: FY2026 standalone revenue ₹3,533.29 crore, PAT ₹24.03 crore and finance cost ₹296.27 crore. Its balance-sheet and financing complexities make it unsuitable as a clean multiple benchmark. Finolex Industries provides a pipes distribution/resin-integration comparison rather than a direct drip-system substitute; its FY2025 annual report states agriculture was 67% of pipes/fittings volumes. Those dated product facts are not assumed FY2026 earnings.

No same-date peer valuation or quality league table is manufactured from these limited primary checks. Substitutes include competing branded systems, local pipe suppliers, low-cost resale and different irrigation methods. Commodity resin exposure, tender/empanelment access, dealer credit and installation service can limit pricing. MOAT 3 recognizes an operating franchise but not protected, high-return economics.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The preselected long window is FY2021 to FY2026: revenue ₹54.5880, ₹37.6227, ₹43.8766, ₹44.4642, ₹13.8884 and ₹45.5811 crore. That is a five-interval CAGR of -3.54%; FY2023 to FY2026 gives 1.28%. The shorter window is shown rather than substituted because it looks better. Revenue rises about 228% in FY2026 only because FY2025 was severely depressed. Absolute FY2026 sales remain below FY2021.

No business acquisition or subsidiary perimeter expansion was identified, so revenue growth is not attributed to an acquired subsidiary. However, a stable legal perimeter is not identical to stable organic product volume: the mix of manufacturing, purchased goods and products changed materially. No price/volume/currency bridge is invented. There is no disclosed export revenue in FY2026; the issuer states customers are in India.

Q1 FY2027 revenue of ₹5.0945 crore compares with ₹0.2619 crore in the prior management-prepared quarter, but remains well below Q4 FY2026 ₹15.2225 crore. Q1 PAT is ₹0.2009 crore after unusually high deferred-tax expense. The current quarter is limited reviewed; the prior quarter was management prepared. Neither the headline growth rate nor a quarter multiplied by four is a reliable annual forecast. The model’s FY2027 annual target explicitly subtracts known Q1 revenue before allocating July–March, and warns that actual seasonality may differ.

The prospectus’s FY2023 largest-customer share was 21.22%, top five 42.78% and top ten 60.50%. FY2026 notes say no customer contributed 10% or more, which is positive concentration counterevidence, although the current top-ten share and common-control relationships are not disclosed. The ₹16 crore Vaira Green arrangement is not counted as a new, collected order book. REV 1 is the schedule outcome; there is no one-point rebound bonus without sufficiently sustained comparable evidence.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
A plant with spare capacity can grow without proportionate machinery spending, but this business has demonstrated a large working-capital requirement. IPO-era capacity utilization was about 11.97% for drip pipes and 5.80% for HDPE pipes in FY2023. Those old figures are not a current utilization estimate. The FY2026 fixed-asset cash addition of ₹1.2353 crore is modest relative to the simultaneous increase in receivables and inventory. Expansion capex is not the main explanation for weak CFO.

The capital test uses normalized operating NOPAT at a 25% analytical tax rate and financing capital equal to equity plus interest-bearing debt less cash, bank deposits, accrued interest and prepaid issue costs. FY2024 financing capital is ₹40.8848 crore and FY2026 ₹65.5745 crore; normalized NOPAT falls by ₹0.442425 crore while capital rises ₹24.6897 crore, giving −1.79% incremental return. The FY2021–26 proxy is 3.91%. FY2025–26 alone improves to 10.57%, but this is a rebound from a loss-year base, not proof of durable high incremental returns.

The FY2026 operating-side cross-check is exact: ₹63.1307 crore operating working capital plus ₹8.4931 crore PPE/intangibles, less ₹5.9851 crore separately identified old obligations and ₹0.0642 crore deferred-tax liability, equals ₹65.5745 crore. Deferred tax is a noncash capital offset, not a modeled cash repayment. The bridge includes customer advances/deposits and retained obligations rather than ignoring free operating funding. Capital proxies are imperfect across Ind AS transition, so conclusions rely on multiple windows and the absolute cash bridge, not a false precision claim about project cohorts.

GQS is 2.15 before and after the applicable ceiling 5. Growth cannot compound owners’ wealth merely by issuing shares and growing resale revenue. The accessible runway would improve if the existing asset base produced sustained collected sales with materially shorter receivable/inventory cycles. Until then, the marginal capital requirement and financing cost constrain the opportunity more than physical plant capacity.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter-led operating team completed the FY2025 preferential financing and a May 2026 warrant conversion, and revenue recovered after the FY2025 collapse. These are real execution facts. At March 2026, the three disclosed promoters held 28.01% in aggregate; that is a dated shareholding figure, not a verified October free-float estimate. Issued shares rose from 11,341,090 before the preferential equity to 22,505,090 at March 2026 and 26,505,090 after the May conversion. Remaining warrants could increase them to 57,601,090. IPO proceeds to the company must be separated from the offer-for-sale proceeds received by sellers.

The ₹17.55 warrant issue comprises ₹4.40 upfront and ₹13.15 at exercise, with an 18 month term from 3 June 2025. The residual call is not simply 31,096,000×₹13.15: June disclosed total warrant receipts exceed the original upfront plus May exercise by ₹0.54796 crore, already received as partial exercise money. Additional future cash is therefore ₹40.34328 crore. Full conversion expands current shares 117.32% and reduces a nonparticipating holder’s percentage ownership 53.99%. Cash received can improve survival while per-share economics still deteriorate.

Related-party disclosures include ₹0.6388 crore director remuneration,22.75% of FY2026 PAT; ₹2.565 crore related-loan repayment; ₹0.5265 crore reimbursements; and ₹0.775 crore related loans outstanding. These are governance-relevant economics, not automatic evidence of diversion. The main audit/CARO reports no fraud noticed and no FY2026 auditor resignation. The earlier IPO record describes an outgoing auditor resignation without reported concerns; it is not erased or inflated into an allegation.

Control discipline remains weak. The FY2024 edit-log facility did not operate. Later reports attest operation and preservation. There were company-secretary vacancies, director/committee gaps, delayed exchange filings and delayed UPSI recording, with management responses describing rectification or paid fines. The specific NSE2024 results delay was two days and ₹10,000 plus GST; a conditional suspension warning is not an actual suspension. Repeated bank-return inconsistencies are more material than that small fine and require a substantive explanation, not a generic compliance assertion.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The main FY2026 audit, CARO and IFC annexures were read separately. The audit is unmodified, IFC is clean, inventory and Ind AS transition are key audit matters, and the report says no FY2026 defaults or wilful-default declaration. Nevertheless, the bank-current-assets table discloses very large unexplained differences. For June/September/December 2025 and March 2026, bank values are ₹104.25/117.82/126.71/127.76 crore versus book values ₹70.00/70.53/103.36/111.29 crore. Stated differences are negative ₹34.25/47.29/23.35/16.48 crore. No reason is filled in. The final quarter has a ₹0.01 crore rounding mismatch, and its stated books ₹111.29 crore exceed audited current assets ₹94.2027 crore by ₹17.0873 crore. The perimeter may differ, but the filing does not explain it. Similar differences recur in FY2023–25. This is the central G2 Hold, not a claim of proven fraud.

Historical defaults must not disappear behind the current clean statement. FY2025 CARO records four loan defaults totaling ₹0.7585073 crore over 9,11,10 and 12 months, with shortage of funds given as the reason. FY2026 reports no defaults. Exact cure dates and renewed facility terms are not verified. Professional tax deducted from employees remained unpaid for extended historical periods; FY2026 still identifies six months of small overdue amounts totaling ₹21,400. Amount and persistence are distinct considerations.

FY2026 reported CFO−₹47.5808 crore includes ₹26.075 crore added to long-dated FDs and a ₹2 crore noncash release of prior prepaid preferential costs. Removing both effects leaves adjusted CFO−₹23.5058 crore. Corresponding investing and financing reclassifications preserve total cash. Reported CFO, investing ₹0.1832 crore and financing ₹48.1952 crore produce net movement ₹0.7977 crore; opening ₹0.1630 crore plus exchange ₹0.0372 crore gives closing ₹0.9979 crore. Issue receipts are not counted twice merely because the prepayment moved through another line. FY2025 restated CFO includes FD release; its balance-movement adjustment is separately identified rather than pretending the old and new cash-flow presentations were identical.

Receivables net ₹52.3054 crore and inventory ₹37.4503 crore are enormous relative to ₹45.5811 crore sales. Receivables older than one year are ₹16.5902 crore,31.46% ofgross balances, while ECL is only ₹0.4329 crore. Auditors highlight third-party inventory. FY2026 material-value-added proxy is ₹14.5842 crore, but this is not disclosed gross profit because labor/production overheads are excluded. Dated-day turnover proxies are embedded with denominator limitations; their magnitude is informative even when an exact cash-conversion cycle cannot be measured.

Other income ₹1.4566 crore includes ₹1.4185 crore interest, roughly 41% of PBT. The FY2025 loss, historical restatements, accumulated working capital and low allowance coverage make reported PAT an uncertain owners-cash proxy. GST claims ₹8.4743 crore, direct-tax contingencies ₹0.1696 crore and guarantees ₹2.1055 crore remain contingent, not automatically payable. Management expects appeal relief; the bear cash model deliberately tests payment of the GST amount.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The reference quote is the actual 19 October NSE bhavcopy close, not a rolling web-page price. ₹49.80×26,505,090 shares gives ₹132.00 crore market capitalization. That is 47.00×FY2026 PAT using current shares. Dividing price by the reported weighted-average EPS ₹1.36 gives 36.62×, but those denominators differ because shares expanded; the lower number is not a current fully diluted P/E. Unconverted warrant money is also part of reported equity, so a casual price/book ratio would mix claims.

Using March debt/cash with October equity, strict diagnostic EV is ₹166.29 crore or 33.37×operating EBITDA. Netting every March FD reduces it to ₹139.83 crore or 28.06×, but that is a sensitivity, not the correct assertion that earmarked/liened deposits are free. No operating land/building value is added on top of earnings EV. There is no NCI in the standalone perimeter. Lease liabilities are not separately presented; missing evidence is not manufactured as a verifiedzero.

The cash model starts at 30 June’s latest published ₹26.1862 crore eligible issue pool, excluding ₹0.0707 crore IPO escrow and not adding stale March cash again. March operating balances and debt are carried to June as explicit assumptions because Q1 has no balance sheet/cash flow. It settles ₹5.9851 crore of old obligations once and models ₹10 crore debt repayment from eligible proceeds, then funds operating costs before each period’s receipts, working-capital changes, capex, tax, interest and scheduled principal. The actual repayments are not asserted to have occurred. Demand-debt rollover is a scenario condition. Fifty/seventy-five/full-percent fund accessibility stresses test lien/use uncertainty.

Bear/base/bull annual FY2027 revenue targets are ₹38/48/55 crore, followed by 0/5/12% growth; EBITDA margins 6/11/14%; target working-capital/revenue 1.65/1.35/1.10 times; capex 2.5/3/4% ofsales; interest 14.6/12/10%; and terminal EV/EBITDA5/8/10 times. Known Q1 revenue is deducted before modeling July–March. Terminal investment continues, a forward operating reserve is retained, residual earmarks can retire debt but are not counted twice as distributable cash, and no cash generated after 20 October 2031 enters shareholder value.

All three core no-exercise paths eventually breach the cash floor. Their conditional returns and hurdle entries are therefore null, even though diagnostic terminal values can be calculated. Separate full-warrant-conversion cases and up-front whole-share rescue cases explicitly show receipts, fees, shares and dilution. The base full-conversion conditional return is-26.7%; it is not an ordinary expected return. The 12/15/18% entry calculations, two-way sensitivities and reverse-growth scans are embedded. No finite funded sign-changing bracket exists for a return-hurdle solution under the tested economics, so no scan endpoint is reported as required growth.

Liquidity is a separate constraint. The latest 20 sessions are all observed: mean turnover ₹2,106,913.75, median ₹863,700 and no explicit zero-trade rows. Across 60 official sessions,59 issuer rows are observed and 29 July is missing, not zero. Their mean is ₹4,431,497.46 and median ₹1,049,500. The unknown nonnegative session bounds the true 60 median between ₹1,032,625 and ₹1,074,312.50; even the minimum possible 60 mean exceeds that interval. Observed-sample theoretical exit is 9.53 days at 5% participation,23.82 at 2% and 4.76 at 10%; the bounded 60 session 5% result is 9.31–9.68 days, not a verified complete-sample point. At ₹49.80 and 500 shares per lot, the ₹500,000 reference floors to 20 lots/10,000 shares/₹498,000 and ceilings to 21 lots/10,500 shares/₹522,900. The observed 5% turnover budget permits only 2 whole lots per day;2% permits less than one lot and 10% permits 4. Those are capacity illustrations, not guaranteed fills. Current free float, spreads, queue depth and a complete surveillance check are unverified. L remains NS.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The bear case is not simply a lower terminal multiple. A subsidy or dealer-collection delay can leave inventory and receivables funded by on-demand debt while salaries, taxes and suppliers still require payment. Aging receivables may be only partly collectible even though they are carried near face value. Inventory at third parties needs existence, title and realizability checks. A lender may reduce drawing power after reconciling submitted current assets, creating cash demand before customers pay. These mechanisms link the bank discrepancy to real funding risk without assuming that a discrepancy itself proves fictitious assets.

The modeled bear case holds annual sales at ₹38 crore, lowers EBITDA margin to 6%, raises the working-capital ratio to 1.65 times, charges 14.6% interest and pays ₹8.4743 crore GST contingency in January 2027. The date and full payment are analyst stress assumptions, not a known demand. Initial disclosed eligible funding supports a finite runway, but the no-exercise path ultimately fails its ₹0.5 crore floor. Funding a rescue does not automatically protect existing equity: the prefunded bear rescue still has zero terminal equity and a−100% conditional return. That is a funded wipeout, distinct from an unfunded path whose return is unscored.

Warrant conversion supplies cash only if holders pay; price above exercise is an economic incentive, not a binding receipt. Exercising all remaining warrants expands the share count 117.32%. The operating business may survive while a current holder suffers major dilution and disappointing per-share value. Further hypothetical rescue equity is issued at an explicit 20% discount to referenceprice with 2% fees, rounded upward to whole shares and received before any modeled cash use. Share expansion and ownership dilution are disclosed separately.

Capital protection requires collections and funded operating continuity, not merely book equity or factory ownership. No liquidation value is assigned to the operating plant on top of earnings value. No credit is given for uncollected claims, speculative partnerships, an unreceived warrant call or undrawn bank headroom that has not been documented.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price outcome requires ₹249 per share and a tenfold outcome ₹498. Over the exact 1,826 day horizon those correspond to about 38.0% and 58.5% annual price returns before costs/tax. These are hurdles, not forecasts or probability estimates.

Dilution changes the hurdle profoundly. At 57,601,090 shares after all existing warrants convert, fivefold and tenfold prices require equity values ₹1434.27 crore and ₹2868.53 crore. Using an explicitly illustrative ₹25 crore net-debt/reserve claim,10×terminal EBITDA and 14% EBITDA margin, required revenue is approximately ₹1042.33 crore and ₹2066.81 crore. Those imply roughly 87.0% and 114.4% five-year growth from FY2026. These are arithmetic requirements, not outputs of the funded operating model.

Physical spare capacity could help some volume growth, but current verified utilization, manufacturing orders, margin mix and subsidy conversion do not support this scale transition. At the modeled working-capital intensity, aggressive growth consumes cash before it creates equity value; simply solving an earnings equation omits the central constraint. Existing warrants alone do not prove that all incremental working capital or capex can be financed, and further equity would raise the per-share hurdle again.

The actual reverse-return routine checks a finite growth scan from−20% to 60%, rejects cash-breaching points, and requires adjacent funded values with opposite residual signs before solving. It found no admissible bracket for the 12/15/18% hurdles. Accordingly there is no defensible numerical required-growth solution within that model. Fivefold/tenfold feasibility is currently unsupported, not declared mathematically impossible under every future business transformation.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The next useful evidence is cash and reconciliation, not another generic irrigation-growth presentation. Obtain a quarter-by-quarter bridge from each bank current-assets submission to the ledger and audited balance-sheet perimeter, with reasons, corrected submissions where applicable and lender acknowledgment. Track old receivable cohorts into actual cash receipts, separate subsidy payors from distributors, and reconcile third-party inventory and related-party settlements.

Before the expected 3 December 2026 warrant deadline, verify every conversion, the incremental cash actually received, partial calls already on hand, current issued shares and any amendment or forfeiture. Do not carry the full optional ₹40.34 crore into a funding forecast merely because exercise would be economically attractive. Reconcile the ₹19.59 crore equity FD and ₹6.59 crore unspent warrant pool to release/lien status, eligible objects and subsequent deployment.

Monitor demand-facility renewal and drawing power, not only total debt. A current no-default statement is positive, but the FY2025 history makes cure dates and recurring repayment performance important. Follow GST appeal status without treating management’s confidence as legal resolution. Require sustained statutory remittance and edit-log operation after the dated remediation.

For business progress, track manufactured versus traded turnover, current utilization, unit realization, dealer sell-through and cash margin. Confirm the Vaira Green arrangement through invoicing and receipts rather than repeating its announced value. Before any trade, replace the illustrative ₹5 lakh reference with the actual intended position, resolve the missing market row and check live lot, restrictions, spreads and queues. These are event-driven research checkpoints, not promises that monitoring or trades have been scheduled.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold for financial reliability, with weak demonstrated business and growth quality. Action: do not initiate a new position on this evidence set. This is not a recommendation to transact in an existing holding and not a claim that the company will fail. Compounder designation: No. BQS 2.84 and GQS 2.15 are analytical diagnostics, not ranking-eligible points; IAS is NS.

The favorable interpretation is that the manufacturing base, product usefulness and repaired control practices allow collections to catch up, while the already-raised eligible funds buy time and optional exercise supplies more capital. The unfavorable interpretation is that accounting profit and new financing continue to substitute for collection and satisfactory incremental returns. The primary record currently supports more caution than confidence.

A lower market price alone cannot clear G2. Reconsideration requires reconciled bank reporting, credible old-receivable recovery, current fund/debt eligibility and a self-consistent plan that remains liquid under realistic timing. The revised analysis must also show per-share value after all funded claims, not just a larger revenue or market-cap figure. If severe diversion or abusive minority conduct were substantiated, the governance override would apply; it is not presumed here.

No ordinary buy range, expected return, price target or position size is provided. Conditional funded scenarios are transparent counterfactuals for understanding the capital structure, not actionable trade levels. The ₹5 lakh liquidity example is a framework reference and does not imply suitability for the user’s finances or portfolio.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The evidence set prioritizes issuer filings and official exchange data: full FY2024–26 annual reports with audit/CARO/IFC/secretarial annexures, the IPO restatements and business risks, June 2026 reviewed results and detailed use-of-funds annexures, preferential/warrant notices and the Vaira Green announcement. Source records retain exact URLs, byte hashes, dates and locators. The financial extracts are analytical transcriptions, not a replacement for the original filings.

Key accounting boundaries are explicit. FY2021/22 use IPO restatements including AS15 adjustments; FY2023 uses the latest comparative with a separate prior-period bridge; FY2024 balance is restated where available; FY2025/26 use the latest Ind AS statements. The FY2023 indirect cash-flow starting line is effectively pre-deferred-tax despite being labeled PAT; deferred tax is not added twice. Cash-flow classification changes, old prepaid issue costs and deposits are reconciled rather than called misconduct by default. Historical ratios use actual fiscal days, including 366 in FY2024.

Forward assumptions are deliberately visible: March operating balances carried to June, eligibility of disclosed issue funds for modeled uses, repayment and renewal conditions, working-capital normalization, margin, capex, tax, interest, terminal multiple and reserves. No private bank balance, unannounced acquisition, current utilization, executable order book or new funding commitment is invented. Optional warrants and hypothetical rescue equity are separate cases. The market row is authenticated, but one missing history session and unverified live execution conditions remain.

The highest-value open questions are the bank-return perimeter and differences; collectibility of old receivables; third-party inventory control; debt cure and renewal terms; FD lien and use restrictions; exact subsequent issue-fund deployment; actual Vaira Green collections; and current manufacturing economics. Resolve these before treating the model as an investment underwriting exercise. Industry policy and peers provide context only, not a substitute for issuer-specific evidence.

summary:
Polysil is not a demonstrated irrigation compounder. The FY2026 revenue rebound to ₹45.58 crore follows a collapse to ₹13.89 crore in FY2025, and remains below FY2021 revenue of ₹54.59 crore. The five-year revenue CAGR is -3.5%. Most FY2026 sales are traded goods rather than internally manufactured output. The important question is collection quality and return on new capital, not the size of India’s irrigation opportunity.

At the authenticated 19 October 2026 close of ₹49.80, current issued equity is worth ₹132.00 crore. BQS is 2.8/10 and GQS 2.2/10; IAS is NS. Financial reliability is on Hold because bank-reported current assets repeatedly differ materially from the books without an adequate explanation. This is not an accusation of fraud. The unmodified FY2026 audit and clean IFC opinion are meaningful counterevidence, but do not reconcile the disclosed differences.

The most consequential adverse facts are persistent cash burn, aged receivables, FY2025 actual loan defaults and substantial dilution. Reported FY2026 CFO of negative ₹47.58 crore overstates operating burn because ₹26.08 crore moved into bank deposits. After that correction and removing a noncash ₹2 crore prepaid-issue-cost release, adjusted CFO is still negative ₹23.51 crore. June disclosures identify ₹26.19 crore of unspent eligible issue funds, while another ₹40.34 crore depends on optional warrant exercise. Full remaining conversion increases current shares by 117.3%.

Do not initiate on the irrigation narrative or the prior share-price decline. The model’s ordinary returns and entry prices are deliberately unscored. Even the separately labeled, funded full-conversion base case generates an illustrative annual return of -26.7%, not an investment target. A repaired bank reconciliation, sustained collections and credible self-funded growth would change the analysis.
